trends.hook: Tripartite recommendations on HR capabilities and AI in hiring (TWG‑HC report)
trends.why_now: Released 24 September 2026; introduces HR certification subsidy (from 1 Oct 2026 to 30 Jun 2028) and guidance on responsible AI in recruitment—notably requiring firms over 200 staff to have IHRP‑CP by July 2028.
trends.source_url: MOM press release on TWG‑HC recommendations, 24 September 2026

trends.why_now: IRAS disbursement begins from 2 Nov 2026 for eligible firms—up to S$2,500 per business based on local employee headcount between April and June 2026.

trends.hook: Labour Market Report 2Q 2026 shows improved hiring intentions
trends.why_now: Report published 21 September 2026 shows firms with hiring plans in next three months rose from 43.9 % in June to 48.7 % in July; total employment growth continued, especially in Professional, Financial Services, ICT, Transportation, Health & Social Services.
trends.source_url: MOM Labour Market Report Q2 2026, 21 September 2026

trends.why_now: As of late 2026, SFEC redesigned: companies with ≥3 resident employees receive S$10,000 fresh credits to immediately offset transformation/course costs; Anchor PPs (SBF, SNEF) appointed for advisory support.
trends.source_url: Factsheet on Enterprise Workforce Transformation Package, late‑2026 redesign

trends.hook: Career Conversion Programme (CCP) support deadlines for hires
trends.why_now: Grants up to 70 % (or 90 % for hires 40+ or long‑term unemployed) per hire under CCP; for hires 4 and 5, letter‑first applications must be filed by 19 Oct and 16 Nov 2026 respectively to meet approval deadlines.
trends.source_url: CCP hiring grants guidance, 7 October 2026 article

recommended.title: AI in Hiring: What Singapore Employers Need to Do Before 2028
recommended.angle: The new Tripartite recommendations mean firms above 200 headcount must certify HR and use AI responsibly—here’s how to avoid compliance headaches, wasted spend, or audit risk.
recommended.why: Singapore’s new tripartite guidelines and HR certification subsidy will directly impact mid-to-large employers’ hiring practices and compliance from 2026 to 2028, requiring urgent planning.

recommended.title: How to Actually Use the 2026 SME Cash Grant to Solve Hiring Gaps
recommended.angle: Most SMEs won’t use this November’s $2,500 cash for staffing—and will miss key opportunities to win growth hires. Here’s how to spend the grant where it actually fixes hiring problems.
recommended.why: The 2026 Cash Grant is about to land for eligible SMEs, giving business owners a rare, time-sensitive lever to address staffing bottlenecks that impact growth.
